LOOK: Human rights advocates, Lumad groups, and ex-political prisoners staged a protest action Wednesday in front of the Department of Justice in Manila to decry the state of the justice system, particularly the incarceration and detention of grassroots leaders in decrepit detention centers.

The deteriorating quality of prisons across the country have led to inhumane conditions for political prisoners. Some elderly peasant organizers have contracted illnesses and have even died behind bars, according to ex-political prisoner Adora Faye de Vera, who is also membered in the Samahan ng Ex-Detainees Laban sa Detensyon at Aresto.

De Vera has been arrested thrice for trumped-up charges. Besides her, there are currently 696 political prisoners in various detention centers in the country, 93 of which are elderly and 89 have contracted serious illnesses, Adora added.

The groups condemned how government officials and contractors embroiled in corruption scandals continue to walk free, while community organizers suffer from state-sponsored violence and red-tagging.
